title: Make React Native builds 4x faster with fingerprint-based caching on Bitrise
summary: Skip the native rebuild when only JavaScript changed. Fingerprint your inputs, cache the output, and cut React Native CI builds from minutes to seconds.
body_markdown:
**Fingerprinting isn't a new idea.** ‍


Build tools have relied on it for years to avoid redoing work that hasn't changed. In React Native CI it's still a bit of a secret sauce: a fingerprint-based caching technique that can make your builds several times faster, yet one that surprisingly few teams have switched on. The premise is simple: most of the time you're only changing JavaScript, so most of the native modules are reusable. Expo's recent[Best CI/CD for mobile apps in 2026](https://expo.dev/blog/best-ci-cd-for-mobile-apps) shows fingerprint-based caching taking an iOS build from roughly 10–15 minutes down to about 2 minutes for a JS-only change. The good news: you don't need anything exotic to get there, just a way to **fingerprint** the inputs and a **cache** to store the output. Here is the flow:


1. **Fingerprint the native inputs** : hash` package.json` , your lockfile,` app.json` , native lockfiles.
2. **Cache restore by that key.** A hit means the last build's native output is valid.
3. **Reuse or rebuild.** On a cache hit, reuse the app and just refresh the JavaScript inside it. Otherwise, do the full native build once and cache it.


*Measured on expo-build-fingerprint-demo: a JS-only change went from ~3.5 min to ~44 s (about 4.8x faster).*


## Fingerprint caching with restore-cache and save-cache


On Bitrise you can wire it up yourself with a bit of scripting. Bitrise's[key-value cache](https://devcenter.bitrise.io/en/dependencies-and-caching/key-value-caching.html) (` restore-cache` /` save-cache` ) ships with the platform. A tiny[open-source step](https://github.com/bitrise-steplib/bitrise-step-react-native-fingerprint) turns your input files into a cache key, and the rest is a few lines of YAML:


```text
-     react-native-fingerprint@0:
inputs:
-     path_list:     |-
package.json
package-lock.json
app.json
-     key_prefix:     build-fingerprint
-     restore-cache@3:
inputs:
-     key:     $BUNDLE_HASH_STRING
```


On a hit you restore the prebuilt, signed app and only refresh the JavaScript inside it. For Android that means swapping` assets/index.android.bundle` in the APK and re-signing; for iOS it's the same move with the JS bundle inside a cached` .xcarchive` (or the simulator` .app` ). Either way, the slow native build stays cached and is skipped on the next JS-only commit.


## Build Cache for React Native: cache compiler outputs, not just the app


The DIY approach is powerful and free. You design the fingerprint, wire the run_if conditions, and do a little IPA/APK surgery (Hermes, assets, re-signing). To make it even better,[Bitrise Build Cache for React Native](https://bitrise.io/platform/build-cache/react-native) gives you an extra boost for speeding up the compilation of native modules with almost no setup.


Setup is a single activate step, with no cache keys or cache objects to manage. Where the DIY approach reuses a finished app, Build Cache goes a level deeper and caches compiler outputs (Gradle tasks, Xcode via an LLVM-CAS-backed cache, C++ via ccache), so even a *dependency* change rebuilds only what actually changed. You also get cache hit rates, time saved, and build analytics out of the box, and the same remote cache speeds up builds on developer machines, not just CI.

## Results: a JS-only change builds 4x faster


The open-source[expo-build-fingerprint-demo](https://github.com/bitrise-silver/expo-build-fingerprint-demo) runs all of this on Bitrise. Here is that app built for iOS **three ways** , on the same` g2.mac.large` machine:

From the results a few things stand out:


- **If it is a JS-only change, skip the native build:** The fingerprint hit avoids the Xcode compile entirely; a 12-second bundle swap instead of a ~1m 47s native build.
- **A genuine rebuild with Bitrise Build Cache support.** When a dependency actually changed, the DIY skip can't help (the fingerprint moved), but Build Cache reduced the Xcode build time, ~2 min down to ~1 min, with a single activate step in the workflow.


They're complementary: fingerprint reuse wins the JS-only case, Build Cache wins the genuine-rebuild case. The same app's Android build shows the same pattern, a JS-only change drops from ~3.5 min to ~44 s.


*Numbers are from the demo app on g2.mac.large; the Build Cache run uses the Xcode 26 stack it requires, so treat them as indicative rather than a lab-controlled A/B.*


### The bigger the app, the bigger the payoff


**‍** This demo is tiny, so a JS-only change saves roughly two minutes. But the swap time stays essentially flat (you're only re-bundling JavaScript), while the native build it replaces grows with your project. Real apps with dozens of native modules often take 10–20 minutes to compile (Expo's own post cites 10–15 minute iOS builds), so the same fast path can turn a 15-minute build into under a minute. Multiply that across every JS-only build your team runs in a week and the savings turn into hours of reclaimed CI time. The ROI scales with your app and your team.


## Faster React Native builds on any CI


Fast React Native CI comes down to one habit: fingerprint your inputs and reuse what didn't change. It's a simple technique, and a surprisingly well-kept one, and on Bitrise you can wire it up yourself in a few lines of YAML. From our experiments it’s about 4x faster on a JS-only change. And because the whole trick is a fingerprint plus a bundle swap, it works on whatever CI you run, Expo or bare React Native, with no lock-in to a single build service. When you'd rather not maintain that plumbing and want observability plus faster dependency-change builds too, Bitrise Build Cache for React Native is the way to go. Ultimately, your builds get faster and you keep the choice.
